problem: The 1871 message (printed in Morris) does not ask for men to be sent 'to treat'; it invites the governor to come and speak with them, asks for provision against starvation, cattle, tools and implements, and states that the land is their property and no one has a right to sell it. The digest omits the land statement.

fix.digest: In the first years after Canada took over the Hudson's Bay Company lands, Sweet Grass and other chiefs sent word to Lieutenant Governor Archibald through W. J. Christie. Their country was being ruined of the fur-bearing animals they lived on; they were poor and wanted help: provision against years of starvation, cattle, tools and implements. They invited the governor to come and speak with them, and said the land was their property and no one had a right to sell it. Morris later printed the message as part of the case that the Cree wanted a treaty.
fix.quote: Make provision for us against years of starvation (as interpreted)
fix.source_note: Message printed in Morris (1880), ch. IX memoranda (AccessGenealogy transcription); DCB, Wikaskokiseyin (year 1871)
